ja: 『モナ・リザ』が世界的に有名になったきっかけの一つは、1911年にルーブル美術館から盗まれた事件だった。
easy: The Mona Lisa became very famous after it was stolen from the Louvre in 1911.
std: The Mona Lisa's worldwide fame grew enormously after it was stolen from the Louvre in 1911.

ja: ゴッホが生きている間に売れた絵は、ほとんどなかったと言われる。
easy: Van Gogh sold very few paintings while he was alive.
std: Vincent van Gogh sold very few paintings during his lifetime.

ja: ミケランジェロはシスティーナ礼拝堂の天井画を、1508年から1512年まで約4年かけて描いた。
easy: Michelangelo spent about four years painting the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
std: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling between 1508 and 1512.

ja: ムンクの『叫び』には、油彩やパステルなど複数のバージョンがある。
easy: There are several versions of Munch's painting 'The Scream'.
std: Edvard Munch made several versions of The Scream, in paint, pastel and print.

ja: ヴィヴァルディの『四季』は、春夏秋冬を表した4つのバイオリン協奏曲。
easy: Vivaldi's 'The Four Seasons' is four violin pieces, one for each season.
std: Vivaldi's The Four Seasons is a set of four violin concertos, each depicting a season.

ja: 日本では年末に「第九」が盛んに演奏される。これほど年末に集中して演奏する国は珍しい。
easy: In Japan, Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is played a lot at the end of the year.
std: Beethoven's Ninth is performed so often in Japan in December that it has become a year-end tradition.

ja: ショパンの心臓は遺言によってポーランドに運ばれ、ワルシャワの教会の柱に納められている。
easy: Chopin's heart was taken to Poland and is kept in a church in Warsaw.
std: At his request, Chopin's heart was taken to Poland and is kept in a pillar of a Warsaw church.

ja: 「ハッピーバースデー」の歌のメロディーは、1893年の「グッド・モーニング・トゥ・オール」という子どもの歌がもと。
easy: The 'Happy Birthday' song came from a children's song from 1893.
std: The melody of 'Happy Birthday to You' comes from 'Good Morning to All', a children's song published in 1893.

ja: ビートルズのシングル『イエスタデイ』は、世界で最も多くカバーされた曲の一つとされる。
easy: 'Yesterday' by the Beatles is one of the most covered songs ever.
std: The Beatles' 'Yesterday' is one of the most covered songs in history.

ja: 歌舞伎は、17世紀初めに出雲の阿国という女性が京都で始めた踊りが起源とされる。今は男性だけが演じる。
easy: Kabuki began with a woman called Okuni in the early 1600s. Today only men act in it.
std: Kabuki is said to have begun with dances by a woman named Izumo no Okuni in Kyoto in the early 1600s; today it is performed only by men.

ja: シェイクスピアは英語に多くの言葉や表現を残した。break the ice（緊張をほぐす）も彼の作品で広まった表現の一つ。
easy: Shakespeare made many English phrases popular, like 'break the ice'.
std: Shakespeare popularized many English expressions, including 'break the ice'.

ja: 世界初の商業映画の上映は、1895年にパリでリュミエール兄弟が行った。
easy: The first public film show for money was in Paris in 1895.
std: The Lumière brothers held the first commercial film screening in Paris in 1895.

ja: 『千と千尋の神隠し』は2003年、アカデミー賞の長編アニメ映画賞を受けた。英語以外の作品で初めて。
easy: 'Spirited Away' won an Oscar in 2003. It was the first non-English film to win this award.
std: Spirited Away won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature in 2003, the first non-English-language film to do so.

ja: 日本の漫画は、ふつう右から左へ読む。英語版でも、元の向きのまま出版されることが多い。
easy: Japanese manga is read from right to left. English versions often keep this order.
std: Japanese manga is read right to left, and many English editions keep the original orientation.

ja: オーケストラは演奏前に、オーボエの「ラ」の音に合わせて音程をそろえる。
easy: Before a concert, the orchestra tunes to an A played by the oboe.
std: Orchestras traditionally tune to an A played by the oboe.

ja: レオナルド・ダ・ヴィンチは、多くのメモを左右反転した鏡文字で書いていた。
easy: Leonardo da Vinci often wrote his notes backward, in mirror writing.
std: Leonardo da Vinci wrote much of his notebooks in mirror writing, from right to left.

ja: ピカソの本名はとても長く、洗礼名を含めると20語以上ある。
easy: Picasso's full name is very long, with more than 20 words.
std: Pablo Picasso's full baptismal name runs to more than 20 words.

ja: 世界で最も訪問者が多い美術館の一つはパリのルーブル美術館で、年間約900万人前後が訪れる。
easy: The Louvre in Paris is one of the most visited museums. About 9 million people go each year.
std: The Louvre in Paris is one of the most visited museums in the world, with around nine million visitors a year.

ja: 『ハリー・ポッター』シリーズは世界で5億部以上売れ、80以上の言語に翻訳された。
easy: The Harry Potter books have sold over 500 million copies in more than 80 languages.
std: The Harry Potter series has sold more than 500 million copies and been translated into over 80 languages.

ja: ゲーム音楽を作曲したすぎやまこういちの『ドラゴンクエスト』序曲は、オーケストラでも演奏され、東京オリンピック2020の入場行進でも使われた。
easy: Music from the Dragon Quest games was played at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics opening.
std: Koichi Sugiyama's Dragon Quest overture was among the video game themes played during the athletes' parade at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

ja: 「?」と「!」を1つにした記号「‽」（インテロバング）は、1962年にアメリカの広告業界の人が考えた。
easy: The symbol ‽ mixes '?' and '!'. It was invented in 1962.
std: The interrobang (‽), combining a question mark and an exclamation mark, was invented in 1962 by an American advertising executive.

ja: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog は、アルファベット26文字すべてを使った文（パングラム）として有名。
easy: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' uses all 26 letters.
std: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' is a famous pangram, a sentence using every letter of the alphabet.

ja: 英語のつづりと発音がずれている理由の一つは、15〜18世紀の「大母音推移」で発音が大きく変わったのに、つづりがあまり変わらなかったこと。
easy: English spelling is strange partly because the sounds of vowels changed a lot 500 years ago.
std: English spelling is irregular partly because of the Great Vowel Shift, which changed pronunciation between about 1400 and 1700 while spelling stayed largely the same.

ja: 英語を話す人の多くは非ネイティブ。英語を使う人の数は、第一言語として話す人よりずっと多い。
easy: Most people who speak English are not native speakers.
std: Non-native speakers of English far outnumber native speakers worldwide.

ja: 英語の color（アメリカ）と colour（イギリス）のつづりの違いは、19世紀にウェブスターが辞書でアメリカ式つづりを広めたことが大きい。
easy: Americans write 'color' and the British write 'colour'. Noah Webster's dictionary made the US spelling popular.
std: American spellings like 'color' instead of 'colour' were popularized by Noah Webster's dictionaries in the 19th century.

ja: アメリカ英語の French fries は、イギリス英語では chips。イギリスの crisps はアメリカでは chips。
easy: Americans say 'fries', and British people say 'chips'. British 'crisps' are American 'chips'.
std: American 'French fries' are British 'chips', while British 'crisps' are American 'chips'.

ja: 車のトランクは、イギリス英語では boot、ボンネットは bonnet（アメリカでは hood）。
easy: A car's 'trunk' is a 'boot' in British English, and the 'hood' is the 'bonnet'.
std: A car's trunk is a 'boot' in British English, and the hood is the 'bonnet'.

ja: 日本語には、英語のように見えて英語では通じない和製英語が多い。たとえば「サラリーマン」「ノートパソコン」は英語では office worker、laptop。
easy: Some English-looking Japanese words are not used in English. A 'salaryman' is an 'office worker'.
std: Many Japanese loanwords that look English are not used that way in English: a 'nōto pasokon' is a laptop.

ja: 和製英語の「クレーム」は、英語では complaint。英語の claim は「主張する・請求する」の意味。
easy: In Japanese, 'kureemu' means complaint. In English, 'claim' means to say something is true.
std: The Japanese loanword 'kurēmu' means a complaint, but English 'claim' means to assert or to demand something as one's right.

ja: 英語でいちばんよく使われる単語は the。上位100語で、書かれた英語の約半分をカバーするとされる。
easy: 'The' is the most common English word. The top 100 words make up about half of written English.
std: 'The' is the most common word in English, and the top 100 words account for roughly half of all written text.

ja: 英語の単語の数は数え方によって大きく変わる。オックスフォード英語辞典の見出しは約50万語以上。
easy: It is hard to count English words. The big Oxford dictionary has about 500,000 entries.
std: Counting English words is difficult; the Oxford English Dictionary contains around half a million entries.

ja: 英語の文の最初を大文字にするのと同じように、ドイツ語ではすべての名詞を大文字で始める。
easy: In German, all nouns start with a capital letter.
std: In German, all nouns are capitalized, not only proper names.

ja: 世界で母語として話す人が最も多い言語は中国語（標準中国語）。話す人の総数では英語が最も多い。
easy: Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers. English has the most speakers in total.
std: Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers, while English has the most speakers overall.

ja: パプアニューギニアでは800以上の言語が話されており、世界で最も言語の種類が多い国とされる。
easy: Papua New Guinea has over 800 languages, the most of any country.
std: Papua New Guinea has over 800 living languages, more than any other country.

ja: 中国語は声の高さの変化（声調）で意味が変わる。標準中国語には4つの声調がある。
easy: In Chinese, the tone of your voice changes the meaning of a word. Mandarin has four tones.
std: Mandarin Chinese is a tonal language with four main tones that change word meanings.

ja: 英語の単語のうち、最も多くの意味を持つ語の一つが run。大きな辞書では数百の意味が載っている。
easy: 'Run' is one of the English words with the most meanings.
std: 'Run' is often cited as one of the English words with the most meanings, with hundreds of senses in large dictionaries.

ja: 赤ちゃんは生まれたときは世界中の言語の音を聞き分けられるが、1歳ごろまでに母語に必要な音に絞られていく。
easy: Babies can hear the sounds of all languages, but by about one year old, they focus on their own language.
std: Infants can distinguish speech sounds from all languages but by around their first birthday become tuned to the sounds of their native language.

ja: 英語の「ほら」「えーと」に当たる um や uh は、世界の多くの言語に似た言葉があり、話の流れを伝える役割がある。
easy: Words like 'um' and 'uh' exist in many languages. They help other people follow the talk.
std: Fillers like 'um' and 'uh' appear in many languages and signal to listeners that the speaker is planning what to say.

ja: 「Huh?（え？）」に似た聞き返しの言葉は、調べた世界の31言語すべてにあったという研究がある（2013年）。
easy: A study found that a word like 'Huh?' exists in all 31 languages it looked at.
std: A 2013 study found a word similar to 'Huh?' used to ask for repetition in all 31 languages examined.

ja: ある文章の95〜98％の語を知っていると、辞書なしで楽に読めるとされる。多読教材が易しめに作られる理由。
easy: If you know 95 to 98 percent of the words, you can read a text easily without a dictionary.
std: Research suggests readers need to know about 95 to 98 percent of the words in a text to read it comfortably without a dictionary.

ja: 猫は甘味を感じる遺伝子が働かず、甘い味がわからないとされる。
easy: Cats cannot taste sweet things.
std: Cats lack a working sweet-taste receptor gene and cannot taste sweetness.

ja: 蚊は、人の吐く二酸化炭素、体温、においなどを手がかりに人を見つける。
easy: Mosquitoes find people by the gas we breathe out, our heat, and our smell.
std: Mosquitoes locate people using exhaled carbon dioxide, body heat and skin odors.

ja: 地球上の砂粒の数より、宇宙の星の数のほうが多いと推定されている。
easy: There may be more stars in space than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches.
std: Estimates suggest the observable universe contains more stars than there are grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches.

ja: 条件によっては、お湯のほうが水より早く凍ることがある。「ムペンバ効果」と呼ばれ、今も研究が続く。
easy: Sometimes hot water can freeze faster than cold water. Scientists are still studying why.
std: Under some conditions hot water may freeze faster than cold, the debated Mpemba effect.

ja: もし地球の歴史を1年にたとえると、人類（ホモ・サピエンス）が現れるのは12月31日の夜11時半過ぎ。
easy: If Earth's history were one year, humans would appear in the last half hour of December 31.
std: If Earth's history were compressed into one year, modern humans would appear in the final half hour of December 31.

ja: 東京スカイツリーの高さ634mは、旧国名「武蔵（むさし）」の語呂合わせ。
easy: Tokyo Skytree is 634 meters tall. The numbers 6-3-4 can be read as 'Musashi', an old name for the area.
std: Tokyo Skytree's height of 634 meters is a pun: the digits can be read as 'Musashi', the region's old name.

ja: カメレオンが体の色を変えるのは、周りに合わせて隠れるためというより、気分や体温の調節、仲間への合図のためが主とされる。
easy: Chameleons change color mostly to show mood or control body heat, not just to hide.
std: Chameleons change color mainly for communication and temperature control rather than simply for camouflage.

ja: 1年が365日ちょうどではなく約365.24日なので、4年に1度うるう年がある。ただし100で割り切れる年は、400で割り切れない限りうるう年にしない。
easy: A year is about 365.24 days, so we add a leap day every four years, with some exceptions.
std: Because a year is about 365.24 days, leap years are added every four years, except century years not divisible by 400.

ja: 地球の自転の遅れを調整するため、時計に1秒を足す「うるう秒」がある。2035年までに廃止されることが決まった。
easy: Sometimes one second is added to clocks, called a 'leap second'. It will stop by 2035.
std: Leap seconds, added to keep clocks in step with Earth's rotation, are set to be abolished by 2035.

ja: ヘリウムを吸うと声が高くなるのは、ヘリウム中では音が速く伝わり、声の響き方が変わるため。
easy: Helium makes your voice sound high because sound moves faster in helium.
std: Breathing helium makes voices sound higher because sound travels faster in helium, changing the resonances of the vocal tract.

ja: カモノハシは卵を産む哺乳類で、くちばしで獲物の出す弱い電気を感じ取れる。
easy: The platypus is a mammal that lays eggs. It can feel electricity from its food.
std: The platypus is an egg-laying mammal that detects prey by sensing weak electric fields with its bill.

ja: 「ブルームーン」は、ひと月に2回目の満月のこと。実際に青く見えるわけではない。
easy: A 'blue moon' is the second full moon in one month. It is not really blue.
std: A 'blue moon' commonly means the second full moon in a calendar month; it does not actually look blue.

ja: アヒルの鳴き声はこだましないという話は誤り。実験で、ちゃんとこだますることが確かめられている。
easy: Some people say a duck's quack does not echo. This is not true.
std: The claim that a duck's quack doesn't echo is a myth; experiments have shown that it does.

ja: 「雷は同じ場所に二度落ちない」は誤り。高いビルには何度も落ちる。エンパイア・ステート・ビルには年に20回以上落ちることがある。
easy: Lightning can strike the same place twice. The Empire State Building is hit many times a year.
std: Lightning often strikes the same place repeatedly; the Empire State Building is hit about 20 times a year.

ja: 金魚の記憶は3秒しかもたないという話は誤り。数か月覚えていることが実験で示されている。
easy: Goldfish do not have a three-second memory. They can remember things for months.
std: The idea that goldfish have a three-second memory is a myth; experiments show they can remember for months.

ja: 「人は脳の10％しか使っていない」という話は誤り。脳のほとんどの部分が何らかの働きをしている。
easy: We do not use only 10% of our brain. We use almost all of it.
std: The idea that we use only 10 percent of our brains is a myth; virtually all brain regions are active.

ja: 闘牛の牛が赤い布に興奮するのは色のせいではない。牛は赤色をよく見分けられず、布の動きに反応している。
easy: Bulls do not get angry because of the color red. They react to the cape's movement.
std: Bulls are not enraged by the color red, which they cannot see well; they react to the cape's movement.

ja: 「砂糖を食べると子どもが興奮する」という考えは、多くの研究で裏づけられていない。
easy: Sugar does not make children hyper. Studies show this is a myth.
std: Many studies have found no evidence that sugar causes hyperactivity in children.

ja: 「コウモリは目が見えない」は誤り。すべてのコウモリは目が見え、多くは超音波も使って周りを知る。
easy: Bats are not blind. They can see, and many also use sound to find their way.
std: Bats are not blind; all species can see, and many also navigate by echolocation.

ja: 世界の人口は2022年11月に80億人に達したと国連が発表した。
easy: The world's population reached 8 billion in November 2022.
std: The United Nations estimated that the world population reached 8 billion in November 2022.
